title: Cybernetics and the Feedback Loop Behind GitOps Reconciliation
explainer: GitOps's core mechanism - a controller that continuously compares a declared desired state against the live state and nudges the system back into alignment - is a direct application of the feedback control loop, the concept Norbert Wiener formalized when he founded the field of cybernetics in his 1948 book 'Cybernetics: Or Control and Communication in the Animal and the Machine.' The same error-correction logic that governs a thermostat or an autopilot is what makes a GitOps reconciler self-healing. Seeing GitOps as a control loop, rather than just 'continuous deployment,' clarifies why convergence and drift detection are central to its design.

title: The 2009 Flickr Talk That Sparked the DevOps Movement
explainer: The platform-engineering and GitOps practices now taken for granted trace back to a specific moment: John Allspaw and Paul Hammond's 2009 Velocity Conference talk, 'Deploys Per Day: Dev and Ops Cooperation at Flickr,' which argued that developers and operators should share tooling and deploy constantly rather than throwing releases over a wall. That talk is widely credited as a spark for the DevOps movement, and by extension for the automated, git-driven deployment pipelines platform teams build today. It is a reminder that GitOps answers a cultural problem first named in 2009, not just a passing tooling trend.
